headline: The new emulator is running, and every tool in the suite now reaches it. It answered a live test call from this session with the right game loaded and 2,674 symbol names available.
matters: The other five lanes can drive it tonight. Anything it cannot do yet refuses by name and stops rather than returning a plausible wrong answer, so we find out what to build next by running into it. Two lanes that had recorded themselves as waiting on you are free to work.
detail: Started target/release/oracle-aether on /run/user/1000/oracle.sock with ../aeon/s4.debug.bin and ../aeon/s4.debug.lst (binding check passed, 2674 symbols). Verified three ways: banner '41 methods advertised'; ss -lxH shows a real LISTEN (not [ -S ], per tonight's stale-socket lesson); and a fresh NDJSON handshake over the socket returns methods=41, serverName=oracle-next, serverVersion=0.0.0, capabilities.breakpoints=false, capabilities.z80=false. End-to-end through the MCP shim confirmed by emulator_status returning romPath '../aeon/s4.debug.bin', the RELATIVE argv only our Rust binary was given, which is aurora's own discriminator against the legacy C++ GUI's absolute path. Loud-failure property demonstrated live: emulator/write_vram returns -32601 'no such method: emulator/write_vram'. Prior state was Errno 2 (ENOENT) with nothing on that path.

headline: The running emulator is now independent of my session. Clearing or restarting me no longer takes it down for the other lanes.
matters: You can rotate or clear this session tonight without knocking five lanes off the emulator. Before this it would have died with me and nothing would have said why.
detail: The server was a direct child of the Claude session (PPID 1905622). Restarted under setsid: PID 2837321, PPID 807 (systemd --user), SID == its own PID, log at /tmp/oracle-aether.log. Re-verified after the move: ss -lxH shows LISTEN on /run/user/1000/oracle.sock, and emulator_status through the shim returns romPath '../aeon/s4.debug.bin'. A second launch attempt refused to bind ('another Aether server is already live') rather than clobbering.

headline: A claim I had been treating as measured turned out to be wrong, and the engine lane caught it. Nothing is broken by tonight's emulator switch.
matters: The job I recommended to you as urgent is not urgent. Nothing is waiting on it and no overnight check is failing. I have re-ranked and put the choice back to you with honest reasons.
detail: aeon traced their own gates: launcher.py:11 spawns the LEGACY oracle_gui into a mkdtemp with an isolated XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so all 9 gate files use private sockets and none reaches the shared server. Verified firsthand. Exposure had been inferred from which methods the gates call rather than which server answers them, and carried under the word 'measured' for two days.

headline: The shared emulator went down when the machine rebooted, and nothing noticed. It is back up and every lane's tools reach it again, with no session restarts needed.
matters: All six sessions booted this morning into a suite whose one shared instrument was silently absent, and each would have found out separately by hitting a failed call. Protecting it from a session rotation last night did not protect it from a reboot — the hub has put the supervision question to you as their own decision.
detail: Reboot at 2026-08-23 23:14 local killed pid 2837321. Measured before acting: /run/user/1000/oracle.sock ENOENT, zero oracle listeners in ss -lx, pid absent, uptime -s confirming the reboot. Restarted target/release/oracle-aether ../aeon/s4.debug.bin --socket /run/user/1000/oracle.sock --symbols ../aeon/s4.debug.lst under setsid: pid 29281, PPID 813 = user systemd, SID = own pid. Verified three ways: banner '41 methods advertised' + 2674 symbols bound to the image; ss -lxH shows a real LISTEN (not [ -S ], per the stale-socket lesson); end-to-end through the MCP shim, emulator_status returning the RELATIVE romPath '../aeon/s4.debug.bin' — the discriminator against the legacy C++ GUI's absolute path. Corrected empyrean's inference that the six live oracle_mcp.py clients were bound to a dead path: oracle_mcp.py _get_bus() constructs a fresh BusClient whenever _bus is None or disconnected, and aether.py:100 resolves the path in __init__, so resolution is per-attempt and no lane needed relaunching. Also fixed lane-status.json, which the Dominion console had been rejecting wholesale since ~02:41Z for carrying a state value the contract does not define, making this lane invisible on the board.

headline: The timing fault you picked is fixed. Our speed measurements could report an interrupt costing more than the whole frame that contained it — now each frame is charged what actually ran in it.
matters: Anyone reading our per-frame speed figures was at risk of chasing a spike that had been moved there from the frame before. The engine team had three measurement tools held back over this; they can now judge whether to move them. The fix also turned up that a feature they asked us to build would not have given them what they wanted, so I have flagged it rather than building it.
detail: Q-PROF-STRADDLE settled as a DEFECT (fork A), merged 51143a5 from branch prof-straddle. Root cause: the per-frame ring cut hintCycles/vintCycles from pending_buckets[level].cycles, an INCLUSIVE figure, and inclusive time only reaches a parent when the callee pops. Because the acknowledge arms a routine frame for the handler's own entry address, a bucket's ENTIRE cost is child time and none reaches the bucket before the RTE — so a straddling handler gave frame N the exception entry alone and frame N+1 the whole span. Fix charges the split on the self side via Frame::enclosing_bucket (stack index of innermost bucket, O(1) at push) + Profiler::pending_bucket_retired, accumulated only while the ring is armed. VERIFIED FIRSTHAND AT THIS SEAT, not accepted on report: full workspace suite 1809 passed / 0 failed / 6 ignored exit 0; red-first REPRODUCED by checking out 68461a7 into a scratch worktree and running it — 37 passed / 2 failed with failure output showing vint_cycles 40 against frame cycles 30, and 80 against 50, i.e. an interrupt costing more than its containing frame, which is what makes it arithmetic rather than taste; merged tree re-verified 41/0. Currency unmoved — golden_frames 7/0, scanline goldens, conformance_roms 3/0 in 41.7s of real work (checked for the silent-skip failure this repo has booked; vendor symlink present, no SKIP markers), schema_conformance 21/0 so no wire drift. RETRACTIONS the agent made against our own records, both correct: the mechanism doc's own SS2 'correction' was wrong (it reasoned from the generic parent/child rule and never asked what a bucket's children ARE), so the original SS3.3(a) finding was right; and SS3/SS6 rested on 'a bucket's cyclesSelf is lag-free', which is true and useless — corroborated by a PRE-EXISTING test, a_nested_hint_inside_a_vint_charges_the_inner_bucket_alone, pinning hint.self_cycles at one STEP_CYCLES against hint.cycles of three. That undercuts PROF-RING-SELF as specified; recommendation to refuse recorded, owner's call, not built. Also merged: new overseer bar that agents must not edit lane-status.json, after this one wrote an enum the suite contract does not define.

headline: Your ruling is built: every hand-driven emulator tool now opens its own copy of the new Oracle and closes it when the session ends.
matters: A machine reboot can no longer take the debugging tools away from all six sessions at once, which happened twice this week. Sessions started from now on get the new behaviour; the ones already open keep working the old way until they restart. Each session also reports which emulator is answering it.
detail: oracle-old main 07314aa + 90f40b8 (fast-forward from branch ephemeral-spawn). Verified firsthand: pytest 11/0/0 rerun at this seat; own spawn witnessed (pid, private /tmp/oracle-mcp-* dir, romPath aeon/s4.debug.bin, reap removed proc+dir, no strays). Default = own instance; ORACLE_SOCKET/EXODUS_SOCKET = explicit attach; the well-known $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/oracle.sock is never dialled implicitly. emulator_status gains an additive 'bus' key {mode, pid, socket, alive}. Spawned server starts paused (oracle-aether default; emulator_resume runs it). Hazards found: fresh 'pip install mcp' resolves to 2.x whose Server lacks list_tools -> requirements now pins mcp<2; mcp.json.sample still names the pre-rename oracle/linux-port path (left alone). oracle-old has no reachable remote, so this lands on disk only.

headline: The new emulator window is now called Oracle and carries the Oracle mark, so it no longer looks like Aurora or the old emulator.
matters: On your desktop the icon shows straight away when the player is run with --x11; on the default Wayland window it shows once the one-line installer has been run, because that windowing layer only lets the desktop entry decide icons. The reason it showed Aurora's icon was measured and was not what anyone guessed: our window had no identity at all, and the task bar grouped it with whatever was nearest.
detail: oracle main merge 1000472 (ae2485c asset + gen script; f6c746a icon.rs, title 'Oracle — frame N', _NET_WM_ICON + XSetClassHint on X11, --x11 flag; 62ccbab .desktop + install-desktop.sh + README). Verified firsthand: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean both feature variants, frontend 250/0/1, merged workspace 51 legs 1812/0/6, zero currency movement, red-first shown (blank-icon poison fails 'fully transparent'). Measured on Plasma/Wayland: minifb set_icon panics on Wayland and never sends app_id; KWin derives class oracle-frontend from the exe; Aurora is Electron (class electron) so the shared-class hypothesis is dead; residual hypothesis = Plasma task grouping of desktop-file-less windows. Deps: raw-window-handle + x11-dl promoted from transitive to direct, zero new crates. Owner follow-up: run crates/oracle-frontend/assets/install-desktop.sh then relaunch; not verifiable from an agent (must not touch ~/.local).

headline: An independent judge has ruled on the proposal that lets a tool tell which emulator answered it, and which build: adopt, with five required fixes.
matters: Once the fixes go into the shared contract and both emulators serve them, a session can never again mistake the old emulator for the new one, or a stale build for a fresh one — the confusion that cost an evening earlier this week. Nothing is on the wire yet; this is the text being authorised.
detail: docs/2026-08-26-ruling-cr-c.md merged ff f22d128 (branch ruling-cr-c, Fable 5, un-framed). 57 CR claims: 53 held, 2 failed (a paraphrased 'quotation'; a stale blob id in §11.9), 2 unverifiable (the 08-21 binary, the running legacy process).
